paper.title: Risk-Averse No-Regret Learning in Online Convex Games

settings.name_in_paper: Risk-averse online convex game with bandit feedback (CVaR-regret)
unmapped: N-agent repeated game: each agent's random cost J_i(x_i, x_{-i}, xi_i) depends on all agents' actions; regret is per agent against the best fixed own action given the others' played actions
Objective is the CVaR at risk level alpha_i of the random cost (risk-averse), not the expected cost
Each round the agent may play the same action n_t = ceil(b U^2 (T-t+1)^a) times and observe n_t i.i.d. cost samples (multiple bandit samples per round)
Costs convex in own action and L_0-Lipschitz in the joint action for every noise realisation; |J_i| <= U
Learner knows its risk level alpha_i and the cost bound U
The analysis assumes all agents run the same algorithm synchronously with common parameters a, b
settings.definition_quote: We consider a repeated game $\mathcal{G}$ with $N$ agents. At the beginning of each episode, each agent $i$ simultaneously chooses an action $x_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_i}$ from a convex set $\mathcal{X}_i$ and receives a random cost value that is sampled from the cost function $J_i(x_i,x_{-i},\xi_i)$ ... we define the regret (CVaR-regret) for agent $i$ as ${\rm{R}}_{C_i}(T) = \sum_{t=1}^{T} C_i(\hat{x}_{i,t},\hat{x}_{-i,t}) - \min_{\tilde{x}_i \in \mathcal{X}_i} \sum_{t=1}^{T} C_i(\tilde{x}_i,\hat{x}_{-i,t})

symbols.a_samp: sampling exponent a in (0,1): n_t = ceil(b U^2 (T-t+1)^a)

conditions: quantity is CVaR-regret at risk level alpha_i
costs convex in own action, L_0-Lipschitz in joint action, |J_i| <= U (Assumptions 1-2)
tuning: delta = sqrt(D_x U d_i)/(N^{1/4} T^{a/4} sqrt(alpha_i L_0))
eta = sqrt(alpha_i) D_x^{3/2}/(sqrt(L_0 U d_i) N^{1/4} T^{3a/4})

source.label: thm:1
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1 and 2 hold and select $\delta=...$, $\eta=...$. Suppose that $n_t$ is chosen as in equation (1) with $a\in(0,1)$, and the EDF and the gradient estimate are defined as in equations (2) and (3), respectively. Then, Algorithm 1 achieves regret ${\rm{R}}_{C_i}^1(T) =\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (T^{1-\frac{a}{4}})$ with probability at least $1-\gamma$.

results.notes: Regret is in terms of CVaR values (risk-aware), so quantity 'other'. T counts episodes; each episode uses n_t samples, so total samples are ~ b U^2 T^{1+a}. Proof's explicit form recorded as r2.

symbols.alpha_risk: CVaR risk level alpha_i of the agent

conditions: quantity is CVaR-regret at risk level alpha_i
tuning: delta and eta as in Theorem 1

source.label: thm:1
source.quote: Substituting $\delta$, $\eta$ and $B_1$ into the regret bound ... we obtain that ${\rm{R}}_{C_i}^1(T)\leq ...=\mathcal{O}( \sqrt{D_x U d_i L_0}N^{\frac{1}{4}}\alpha_i^{-\frac{1}{2}} \sqrt{\ln(T/\gamma)} T^{1-\frac{a}{4}} )$

results.notes: Explicit form from the proof of Theorem 1; d is the agent's dimension d_i, gamma (failure prob.) mapped to delta, D_x to diam_K, L_0 to L_lip.

tuning: delta and eta as in Theorem 1

source.label: thm:2
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1, 2 and 3 hold, and assume the same values for $\delta$ and $\eta$ as in Algorithm 1 ... Then, when $T>T_{\lambda}$ with $T_{\lambda}$ as in Lemma 7, Algorithm 2 achieves regret ${\rm{R}}^2_{C_i}(T)< Err(\text{ZO})+ Err(\text{CVaR})$ and thus ${\rm{R}}^2_{C_i}(T)= \tilde{\mathcal{O}} (T^{1-\frac{a}{4}})$.

results.notes: Theorem statement does not repeat the probability, but it relies on Lemma 7 holding w.p. at least 1-gamma. Strictly smaller than Algorithm 1's bound. Corollary 1 (hybrid sampling with switching time t_0) gives the same Õ(T^{1-a/4}) for T > T_lambda(t_0); not recorded separately.

source.label: thm:3
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1 and 2 hold, and select $\eta=\frac{D_x }{d_i L_0 N}T^{-\frac{3a}{4}}$, $\delta=\frac{D_x }{ N^{\frac{1}{6}}}T^{-\frac{a}{4}}$. Suppose that $n_t$ is chosen according to equation (1) with $a\in(0,1)$ ... Then, when $T\geq (8N^{\frac{2}{3}} )^{\frac{1}{a}}$, Algorithm 3 achieves the regret ${\rm{R}}^3_{C_i}(T) =\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (T^{1-\frac{a}{4}})$ with probability at least $1-\gamma$.

symbols.S_alpha: S(alpha) = sum_i 1/alpha_i^2 over agents' risk levels

source.label: thm:3
source.quote: More precisely, Algorithm 3 actually achieves the regret ${\rm{R}}^3_{C_i}(T)= \mathcal{O}( D_x d_i L_0 NS(\alpha) \ln(T/\gamma) T^{1-\frac{a}{4}} )$, where $S(\alpha):=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{1}{\alpha_i^2}$

results.notes: Explicit form stated after Theorem 3 and in Appendix C.2.
